round_interpretation: Round one increased hypervolume by 27.78%. Dropping both HY axes improved all three aggregate objectives; individual flow, rank and acceleration removals generated different sparse tradeoffs. Removing VIX-slope z-score was harmful and annual CPI was not dispensable in the original context. Combine promising removals on the no-HY parent, test remaining local/macro axes directly, and contrast the HY-level-retaining branch. The three-target allocation cap makes small Sharpe differences especially weak evidence.
default_expected_tradeoff: Evaluate complete three-objective and per-seed results; record input savings, calibration and width separately. Do not call a tiny Sharpe difference robust economic improvement.
default_falsification: A dominated result does not support the specified conditional reduction. Keep nondominated tradeoffs and report context dependence rather than compelling one fixed family winner.
